A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AgentScore work. The main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–G support reliable comparison. The shorter bibliography explains the page-count reduction; no appendix material is missing.

before.justification: v2 reports original clinical prediction experiments, external validation, ablations, privacy and robustness tests, and an 18-clinician evaluation in Section 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 reports the same original experimental and clinician-review outcomes in Section 5 and Appendix E, including held-out prediction results and the 18-participant study.

M1.justification: The rule grammar, LLM proposal and plausibility stages, deterministic screening, checklist assembly and refinement, and threshold selection are unchanged in Sections 2 and 4, Algorithms 1–2, and Appendices F–G.

E1.justification: Both retain eight MIMIC-IV/eICU prediction tasks, external validation using PhysioNet 2012 and UK-to-Canadian cystic-fibrosis cohorts, and the same clinician-review scenarios. Appendix D's dataset and task coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Table 3, the guideline comparisons in Figure 3, and the appendix experiments. This includes the representation-controlled comparisons in Table 11 and the clinician study comparing AgentScore with FasterRisk.

E3.justification: The cross-validation and internal validation splits, preprocessing, AUROC evaluation, external-validation procedures, model configurations and clinician-study design are unchanged in Section 5 and Appendices D–E.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 and Appendix E retain the same component and representation-controlled ablations, backbone and checklist-size sensitivity studies, risk-monotonicity analysis, privacy audit, missingness tests and scoring-system analyses.

E5.justification: Fold and seed counts, mean±SD reporting, Holm-corrected model comparisons, bootstrap confidence intervals, effect sizes and clinician-study statistical procedures are unchanged, including Figure 3, Table 12 and Appendix E.9.

E6.justification: The numerical results and findings match throughout the main text and appendices, including AgentScore's Table 3 mean AUROC of 0.71±0.08. Two Table 3 cells gain boldface, but their values and the numerical rankings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The rule and scoring-system definitions, constrained optimization formulations, and complexity arguments in Section 2 and Appendices E.1 and F are unchanged. No formal assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions box and conclusion retain the same claims about joint rule construction and selection, deployable unit-weighted checklists, and predictive competitiveness. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations and qualifications are unchanged, including limited expressivity, knowledge-bounded discovery, absence of global-optimality and formal privacy guarantees, distribution-shift concerns, and the clinician study's limited generalizability.

D1.justification: Experimental implementation, hyperparameters, hardware, runtime and cost reporting, data processing, algorithmic details and prompts are unchanged in Appendices D–G. Both code-release links in the impact statement are retained.

R1.justification: The same cited works and research positioning remain, including Section 3 and Appendix C. The bibliography removes DOI and URL fields rather than removing works or changing their relationship to AgentScore.

P1.justification: v3 expands the acknowledgments to thank ICML reviewers, disclose CCAIM's institutional funders, and credit BioRender for Figures 1–2. Bibliographic DOI/URL fields are removed; the scientific prose and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 3 newly bolds Optimal Checklists' unchanged MIMIC Cancer result, 0.62±0.02, and MIMIC Lung result, 0.67±0.01. Acknowledgments and references reflow; other scientific displays and matched appendix layouts are unchanged apart from pagination.

improvement.justification: The added institutional-funding disclosure improves transparency, and Table 3 more accurately highlights two baseline-best results. These are limited gains; the scientific evidence and conclusions remain unchanged. Removing bibliography DOI/URL fields reduces direct lookup convenience, but all cited works remain identifiable.
